sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Bologna's policy has been to make driving in the centre and at 50 km/h dearer, harder and slower. On-street tariffs rose from 2 May 2025: one hour went from 1.80 to 2.90 euros in the historic centre and from 2.40 to 3.90 euros in the innermost Cerchia dei Mille, with monthly permits between 60 and 100 euros and about 5.4 million euros a year of extra income put forward by the Comune [0]. Council figures from October 2025 show parking spaces in the centre falling from 10,098 in 2013 to 9,136 in December 2024, with standard blue-line spaces down from 6,172 to 5,866 in two years while resident white-line spaces rose from 1,110 to 1,271 [6]. The historic-centre ZTL is monitored by electronic gates from 7:00 to 20:00 every day, and the pedestrian zones and the 'area T' are restricted around the clock, according to the tourist office page [2]. A report of 28 December 2025 said that from 1 January 2026 the virtual ZTL permit for hybrid cars would be issued only to residents of Bologna or companies based in the city, so non-resident hybrid owners would need the paid daily ticket; the Comune counted about 10,259 hybrids of non-residents that could no longer be given access, and permits already issued stay valid until they expire [1].

The 30 km/h limit is the contested part. In January 2026 the regional administrative court annulled the blanket 30 km/h limit on city roads, calling it disproportionate; the decision was not final [3]. In March 2026 the Comune approved a new Città 30 plan with a technical sheet for each street, covering 258 km of roads in 47 zones and planned to take effect on 20 April 2026; we did not find a source confirming that it did [4]. The metropolitan mobility plan (PUMS) was approved in November 2019 [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
Bologna is adding capacity at the edge of the centre while shrinking it inside. The ex-Staveco car park on viale Panzacchi reopened on 20 October 2025 after works costing 2.8 million euros, going from just under 180 to about 300 spaces; tariffs stayed at 2 euros an hour by day, 1 euro at night and 12 euros a day, and an electronic toll was planned for November 2025 [7]. The works were announced in 2024 with the operator Bomob, whose cost was to be deducted from the fee it pays the Comune [8]. A dispute concerns the Tanari car park beside the station, which belongs to FS Sistemi Urbani, which was asking the Comune to hand it back; in January 2026 it was reported open but unstaffed and degraded, with a mediation meeting planned [9]. The interchange car parks at Prati di Caprara, Antistadio, Ferriera and others are free only in combination with a bike or a bus ticket [15].

The trams are the bigger change. The Green Line plan reported in 2024 included a 200-space multi-storey car park and 197 surface spaces along the route, with works to June 2026 [16]. The first Red Line tram was unveiled on 9 September 2026, and the mayor said the aim is to be ready in spring 2027, subject to national approval [17]. The Comune's open data list 129 EV charging locations with 235 bays, 128 active, operated mostly by Be Charge, Enel X and Hera [14].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The Comune's own data set lists 44 car park facilities, from Michelino (5,500 spaces) and the new station car park (900) to Riva Reno (543) and Autostazione (280) [13], and publishes availability readings every 10 minutes for three garages [12]. APCOA operates Piazza VIII Agosto, with 702 spaces, 3.30 euros an hour for hours one to three and a daily maximum of 25 euros [10], and apparently Riva Reno, which has 546 spaces and remote customer assistance [11]; we did not establish who operates the Autostazione garage. Tper's and other operators' roles were not found.

Our data cover exactly those three garages, from the Comune's feed, for 61 days since 22 August 2026. The feed's capacities are lower than the operator and dataset figures: 625 for VIII Agosto against 702, 470 for Riva Reno against 546 and 257 for Autostazione against 280. Occupancy averaged about 45% on weekdays and 49% at weekends, weighted by spaces, so Bologna's garages are not quieter at weekends. VIII Agosto is the fullest at 51% on weekdays and 55% at weekends, Riva Reno 41% and 44%, and Autostazione 35% and 43%. All three reached full in single readings, on a Friday in the case of VIII Agosto and Riva Reno. These are three garages out of 44, so they say little about the city as a whole, and the window starts in late summer.
